title: Foley (Indwelling Urinary) Catheter Insertion
summary: Inserting a sterile indwelling urinary catheter to drain the bladder.
equipment: Sterile Foley catheter kit (includes catheter, drape, betadine, lubricant, syringe, collection bag)
steps: Verify provider order. Explain procedure to patient and provide privacy.
Position patient: female — dorsal recumbent (frog-leg); male — supine.
Perform hand hygiene. Open catheter kit using sterile technique.
Don sterile gloves. Organize sterile field — open all supplies onto field.
Place sterile drape under the patient's buttocks and fenestrated drape over the perineum.
Female: Separate labia with non-dominant hand (this hand is now contaminated). Use dominant hand to cleanse urethral meatus with betadine swabs — front to back, center, then each side.
Male: Hold penis with non-dominant hand perpendicular to body. Retract foreskin if present. Cleanse meatus in circular motion from center outward.
Lubricate catheter tip. Insert catheter gently into urethra — female: 2–3 inches; male: 6–9 inches — until urine flows.
Advance 1–2 more inches after urine appears. Inflate balloon with sterile water per catheter size (typically 10mL).
Gently pull back until resistance is felt — confirms balloon is in bladder.
Secure catheter to inner thigh. Connect drainage bag and position below bladder level.
Document insertion, initial urine output, color, clarity, and patient tolerance.
nursing_considerations: Use CAUTIs bundle: insert only when medically necessary, use aseptic technique, reassess need daily.
Never force the catheter — if resistance is met, stop and notify provider.
Replace foreskin to original position after insertion (prevent paraphimosis).
Assess for CAUTI symptoms: fever, cloudy/foul urine, suprapubic pain.
Remove catheter as soon as no longer clinically indicated to reduce infection risk.

title: Straight (In-and-Out) Catheterization
summary: Temporarily inserting a urinary catheter to drain the bladder once, then removing it immediately.
equipment: Straight catheter kit (catheter 14–16Fr, drape, cleanser, lubricant)
steps: Verify provider order and indication (urinary retention, post-void residual check, urine specimen).
Explain procedure to patient. Ensure privacy.
Position patient same as for Foley insertion (female dorsal recumbent, male supine).
Perform hand hygiene. Open catheter kit using sterile technique on a clean surface.
Don sterile gloves. Set up sterile field.
Cleanse the urethral meatus using the same technique as Foley insertion.
Lubricate catheter. Gently insert straight catheter into urethra until urine flows.
If obtaining a specimen: collect urine mid-stream into specimen container using sterile technique.
Allow bladder to fully drain into basin. Note total volume.
If PVR (post-void residual): drain completely and record volume.
Once drainage is complete, pinch the catheter and withdraw smoothly.
Cleanse perineal area. Make patient comfortable.
Document volume drained, urine characteristics, and patient tolerance.
nursing_considerations: Post-void residual (PVR) >150–200 mL is generally considered significant — report to provider.
Do not drain more than 500–1000 mL at one time (facility-dependent) to prevent rapid decompression vasovagal response.
Straight catheterization has a lower infection risk than indwelling catheter — preferred when temporary drainage is sufficient.
If patient has a history of urethral stricture or prostate enlargement, notify provider before attempting.
Maintain strict sterile technique — even single-use catheters can introduce bacteria if contaminated.

title: Bladder Ultrasound Scan (PVR Assessment)
summary: Non-invasive ultrasound measurement of bladder volume to assess post-void residual or urinary retention.
steps: Verify order or protocol (e.g., assess PVR, suspect urinary retention).
Explain procedure to patient — painless and non-invasive.
Ask patient to void before scan (if measuring PVR). Scan within 10–15 minutes of voiding.
Position patient supine. Expose lower abdomen just above the pubic bone.
Perform hand hygiene and don gloves.
Turn on bladder scanner. Select patient gender (affects scan algorithm).
Apply ultrasound gel to the scan head.
Place the scanner head approximately 1 inch above the pubic symphysis, aiming toward the bladder (angled slightly toward the coccyx).
Press the scan button. Hold the probe steady until the device beeps and displays volume.
If volume is ≥300 mL or as ordered, repeat scan for confirmation.
Wipe gel off patient's abdomen with gauze.
Document scan volume, number of scans, timing relative to voiding, and clinical action taken.
nursing_considerations: Bladder scanner may overestimate volume in obese patients or those with ascites — use clinical judgment.
Scanning over a uterus (pregnant or fibroid) may falsely elevate results — note in documentation.
A single scan may vary ±15% — perform 2–3 scans and average, or use highest consistent reading.
PVR >200 mL typically warrants straight catheterization and provider notification.
Do not delay catheterization in a patient with obvious urinary retention symptoms (distended bladder, severe discomfort, no urine output) just to scan first.

title: Urinary Ostomy (Urostomy) Pouch Change
summary: Emptying and replacing a urinary ostomy (ileal conduit) pouching system.
equipment: One-piece or two-piece urostomy pouch system
Skin barrier paste or powder (if needed)
Warm water and gentle soap or no-rinse cleanser
steps: Gather all supplies. Perform hand hygiene and don gloves.
Empty the pouch by opening the tap/valve and draining into the toilet before removing.
Gently remove the old pouch: push skin down and away while lifting the pouch up — do not rip.
Note stoma color, size, and condition. Observe peristomal skin for redness, erosion, or yeast.
Cleanse the stoma and surrounding skin with warm water. Pat dry completely — moisture prevents seal.
Measure the stoma with a guide. Cut the skin barrier opening to the correct size (2–3 mm larger than stoma).
Apply skin barrier paste or powder to peristomal skin if irritation is present.
Apply skin prep wipe and allow to dry to create a tacky base.
Remove backing from the skin barrier. Center over stoma and press firmly for 30 seconds.
For a two-piece system, attach the pouch to the flange, pressing around the entire ring to seal.
Ensure drainage tap/valve is closed. Smooth out any wrinkles in the pouch.
Document stoma appearance, pouch change, output color and amount, and peristomal skin condition.
nursing_considerations: A healthy stoma should be beefy red/pink and moist — pale, dark, or black stoma requires immediate provider notification.
Change pouch every 3–5 days or sooner if leaking — prolonged contact of urine with skin causes severe irritation.
Mucus shreds in urostomy drainage are normal (ileal mucosa still produces mucus).
Avoid oil-based lotions near the stoma — they prevent the pouch from adhering.
Teach patient/family self-care before discharge — ostomy management is primarily a self-care skill.
